comments.body: I'm guessing it is because we don't know how to take a subview in some cases. Would the subview be in the middle of a swizzling pattern. I'm surprised we support subview for this layout actually but I think we need to consider the layout when calculating the subview offset?
Happy to take a look tonight. How do I reproduce the issue? @bingyizh233

> > Happy to take a look tonight. How do I reproduce the issue? [@bingyizh233](https://github.com/bingyizh233)
> 
> Thank you so much! I will send a reproducer soon.

I just create a reproducer for it https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer  which is modify from triton toturial for GEMM

In this reproducer, there are two cases:

(float-32 Block-K32)  which will produce correct results after subtiling: https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/float32-K32/modify/VCXEA46VQKHIJWBSGWBSUPKR2UHBSKLJEIAMSPO5KU4X5C2ORVRA/matmul_kernel.ttgir#L130-L148

(float-32 block-K64) which will produce **in**correct results afer subtiling:
https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/float32-K64/modify/E5AUXTEOVSC2HLBIYGCUYMHDDZYKU37A3XAEFLQZM6Q2SXJLUKNA/matmul_kernel.ttgir#L130-L168

We can comment/uncomment the env var to control overwrite: https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/float32-K64/matmul.py#L11-L18

Without subtiling, both cases will give correct results.


Let me know if you any additional information for reproducing the issues. Thanks a lot!

I find more clues through comparing the ptx:
without subtiling (results are correct, normal): https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/ptx/float32_K64_normal.ptx
with subtiling (results are incorrect, bug): https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/ptx/float32_K64_bug.ptx

The two ptxes are easy to compare, both use %r958 for base address of matrix A and use %r960 for the base address of matrix B


In normal ptx https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/ptx/float32_K64_normal.ptx
We can see the offsets for each WGMMA: https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/ptx/float32_K64_normal.ptx#L1903-L1980

such as 
```
	add.s64 	%rd367, %rd478, 4611686293372403714;
	add.s64 	%rd368, %rd480, 4611686293372403714;
```
4611686293372403714 is the offset added to descriptor 


In bug ptx https, we can also see the offsets for each WGMMA  https://github.com/bingyizh233/Reproducer/blob/main/ptx/float32_K64_bug.ptx#L1899-L2106


I used gpt-4o to help me calculate some of the values.  paste some of ptx to  gpt-4o. Tell it to suppose  %r958=0 and use %r960=0. I find half of the descriptor  of normal ptx and bug ptx does not match. 
 
For example, 	in wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64n128k8.f32.tf32.tf32 {%f2959,%f2960,%f2961,%f2962,%f2963,%f2964,%f2965,%f2966,%f2967,%f2968,%f2969,%f2970,%f2971,%f2972,%f2973,%f2974,%f2975,%f2976,%f2977,%f2978,%f2979,%f2980,%f2981,%f2982,%f2983,%f2984,%f2985,%f2986,%f2987,%f2988,%f2989,%f2990,%f2991,%f2992,%f2993,%f2994,%f2995,%f2996,%f2997,%f2998,%f2999,%f3000,%f3001,%f3002,%f3003,%f3004,%f3005,%f3006,%f3007,%f3008,%f3009,%f3010,%f3011,%f3012,%f3013,%f3014,%f3015,%f3016,%f3017,%f3018,%f3019,%f3020,%f3021,%f3022}, %rd365, %rd366, %p38, 1, 1;


%rd365 and %rd366 are descriptors for this wgmma.


I find that the descriptors of first half subtiles match. However, the descriptor of the second half subtiles does not match.


Currently, not sure why it does not match. I guess we may need to update the logic for calculating the offset/descriptor to support subtiling cases.

@bingyizh233 please skip comparing PTX as I feel it will be waste of time. Which version of triton should I use?

I reminded now that it's a high level problem that I didn't consider shared memory offsets when the encoding has a leading dimension. Back to the time we thought slicing will not be enabled for such cases. I should have left an assert for better debugging though...

> [@bingyizh233](https://github.com/bingyizh233) please skip comparing PTX as I feel it will be waste of time. Which version of triton should I use?
> 
> I reminded now that it's a high level problem that I didn't consider shared memory offsets when the encoding has a leading dimension. Back to the time we thought slicing will not be enabled for such cases. I should have left an assert for better debugging though...

Thanks! I am using the newest triton. You can use the newest triton. It should reproduce the issue.

Theoretically, the subtiling will works for Hopper. Actually, most cases are already working. Because for Hopper, the subtiles (e.g., 64x16) in a tile (e.g., 64x64, swizzled in k dim) using the same descriptor configuration (leading dimension offset, stride dimension offset) except the base address (the address of the first element in a subtile).  As long as we provide correct base address in the descriptor, wgmma will be able to fetch the data correctly.   

FYI, the shared memory descriptor: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#tcgen05-shared-memory-descriptor

@Jokeren  Just want to clarify. We just need to breakdown the wgmma along numRepK dimension https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/main/third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/DotOpToLLVM/WGMMA.cpp#L391   This is what 'subtiling meaning" here, each subtile is a piece in numRepK dimension.  I think triton do it correctly when generating numRepK together in a single wgmma op.   But if we break numRepk down into several wgmma op, it give incorrect in some cases.  This is what I reported here.
I think it's not a bug triggered by the WGMMA file itself. Instead should be the code related with memory subview

> This is what I reported here.

Yeah it's clear to me

> I think it's not a bug triggered by the WGMMA file itself. Instead should be the code related with memory subview

I see. It could be that. For the k dimension, when shared memory swizzle size < matrix size (k).  Data loading will load the first tile of shared memory swizzle size, then next tile of shared memory swizzle size. However, subview always assume (stride == matrix size).

Have confirmed that when shared memory swizzle size < matrix size (k), some cases will generate incorrect results. Because in this case, subview does not calculate correct bases address for some subtiles. Currently, disabled the subtiliting + prefetching optimization when shared memory swizzle size < matrix size (k) in https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/6196.     

In the future, it could be fixed in subview.

> In the future, it could be fixed in subview.

Oh, I'm working on the fix now
It could be a separate PR though. Will pin you tomorrow

> It could be a separate PR though. Will pin you tomorrow

Thanks!
Reopening as this looks like a thing we'd like to fix.

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

This bug is found when creating the PR: https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/6196

The issue is on Hopper when performs  matrix multiplication:    A x B -> C using  wgmma

A simple bug description/reproducer is that:

Both A, B, C  are float32 data format.
A has the shape  128  X  K ,   float32
B has the shape   K x 128,  float32

For A x B -> C,  suppose k = 32
we can break it down to subtile in ttgir such that:
C = 0
A1 = subview [0, 0]  with shape  128x16
B1 = subview [0, 0]  with shape  16x128
C += wgmma(A1 x B1)  
A2 = subview [0, 16]  with shape  128x16
B2 = subview [16, 0]  with shape  16x128
C += wgmma(A2 x B2)  

when K = 32, such change will produce correct results.



However, when K  = 64, we break it down into subtiles:

C = 0
A1 = subview [0, 0]  with shape  128x16
B1 = subview [0, 0]  with shape  16x128
C += wgmma(A1 x B1)  
A2 = subview [0, 16]  with shape  128x16
B2 = subview [16, 0]  with shape  16x128
C +=  wgmma(A2 x B2)
A3 = subview [0, 32]  with shape  128x16
B3 = subview [32, 0]  with shape  16x128
C +=  wgmma(A3 x B3)  
A4 = subview [0, 48]  with shape  128x16
B4 = subview [48, 0]  with shape  16x128
C +=  wgmma(A4 x B4)  

It will produce incorrect results.  Change subtitle size 16 to 8 or 32 will also produce incorrect results.


In the above cases, both A and B comes from shared memory, described by the memory descriptor.


There might be potential issue for subview or  WGMMA.cpp when creating memory descriptor for hopper subtilting.


Currently, find the bug exist for databitwidth=32 and  K >=64.




@ThomasRaoux  @lezcano  Wondering if you have any clues for this bug or where the bug could come from?








### Environment details

Hopper 100
